description:
Goal: in a hot loop, every instruction fz emits is one the operation needs. These costs appear in EVERY listing of the binary machine-code study (fz-9e2 materials, /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-binaries/machine.md, M9 and M12-M14), not only binary ones. The empty loop `loop(n - 1, acc + 1)` is 22 instructions per iteration, and about 12 of those are avoidable.

Method (the same as fz-9e2, user 2026-11-18):
1. Hand-write the optimal arm64 target listing first, annotating each instruction with the fact that licenses it.
2. Then make Cranelift lowering emit that listing.
3. Judge on bench (ssh bench, BENCH_BUSY lock); local slopes are iteration aids only.

Probes and harness: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-binaries/listings/probes (m.sh slope, tr.sh + trace.py lldb single-step); listings per probe in /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-binaries/listings. fz-9e2.1 moves the harness into the repo; share it, do not build a second one.

Concordant and already owned (not children here):
- fz-9x7.39 and Callables' continuation page step B: a capture slot's store and restore are specialized by kind. M9 measured 9-20 instructions per lane, three times per binary lane across a non-tail call.
- fz-sc8.249: callee-saved register traffic in leaves.
- fz-nml.9: an integer sent in a message is heap-boxed (M12: send of an int is 289 instructions more than send of a binary).

Acceptance: each child's emitted listing matches its target, and the empty-loop probe p00 falls from 22 instructions per iteration to the target count.
title: In a hot loop every instruction is one the operation needs
